body:
Greg's direction, relayed by Engram::Advisor (TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #2878, 2026-10-31T15:49:19Z), verbatim: „Greg: DL560 ma 72 cory i 256 GB pamieci; jego zdaniem nie wymaga synchronizacji dostepu i powinien obslugiwac rownolegle zadania. Prosze usunac sztuczny jeden slot na DL560 i zaplanowac rownolegle niezalezne gate i cargo, z osobnymi worktree/targetami i rozsądnymi limitami faktycznych zasobow; potwierdzic praktyczne wykorzystanie."

Operating rule (Termal::Fable2, from 15:50Z):
- DL560 is NO LONGER one-job-at-a-time. Independent gates and cargo jobs run in parallel, each in its OWN worktree with its OWN target dir; nothing is shared.
- Limits, checked by a census at each launch:
  - at most 3 concurrent jobs (full or focused);
  - start a new one only if MemAvailable ≥ 64 GiB, disk ≥ 100 GB and the 1-minute load is below 100;
  - with 2 or more running, give each new job CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=48 so 144 threads aren't oversubscribed.
- Each GO is still named, per job, with the input identity and fingerprints before and after.
- A failure under concurrency is still investigated as a failed gate. Concurrency is a hypothesis to test, not a licence to retry.
- Central Windows stays one Cargo job at a time; this direction covers DL560 only.
- This supersedes the quiet-host one-slot assumption for DL560 only.
